name: Joel and Abiah, the sons of Samuel
charge: Turning aside after lucre, taking bribes, and perverting judgment in the seat of the judge
summary: When Samuel was old he made his sons judges over Israel in Beersheba, and they did not follow his ways: they chased dishonest gain, took bribes, and perverted justice. The elders of Israel used them as the reason to demand a king like all the nations. No sentence upon the two men is recorded anywhere in the chapter; the sentence that is recorded fell on the nation that used them as an excuse.
offenseFull: When Samuel was old he made his sons judges over Israel, Joel the firstborn and Abiah the second, judging in Beersheba. But his sons did not follow his ways: they chased dishonest gain, took bribes, and perverted justice (1 Samuel 8:1-3). The law for the judges in the gates was plain. They were to judge the people justly, not twist judgment, not show partiality, and take no gift, because a bribe blinds even the wise and corrupts the cause of the righteous (Deuteronomy 16:18-20; Exodus 23:8). That gift is what goes into the pocket of a judge and comes back out as a perverted sentence against the man who could not pay.

We see that same thing going on now in this political climate, and even in the church system. It is why the churches will not teach us who we are or teach the commandments of the Most High, and why, when riots and unrest break out, it is those same pastors who are sent out to calm the people down. The contrast with their father was public and undeniable. Samuel could stand before all Israel and ask whose ox or donkey he had taken, whom he had cheated, and from whom he had taken a bribe, and the whole congregation answered that he had taken nothing from anyone (1 Samuel 12:3-4). The sons made the seat of judgment serve their own increase.
judgmentFull: Then all the elders of Israel came to Samuel at Ramah, saying he was old and his sons did not follow his ways, and asking him to appoint a king to judge them like all the nations (1 Samuel 8:4-5). Your sons are not righteous like you, so instead of them judging us, give us a ruler like the other nations have. The corruption was real and the complaint was real; the remedy the people insisted on is its own case, entered next, because the Lord told Samuel that they had not rejected him but had rejected the Lord as their king (1 Samuel 8:7).

No penalty upon Joel or Abiah is recorded. Their own end is not written, and the silence does not turn bribery into righteousness. If a man sees the poor oppressed and justice violently perverted in a province, he is not to be astonished, for a higher official watches over the high one, and One higher still is over them both (Ecclesiastes 5:8). What the record does show is the damage: an office handed down without the character the office requires, a nation that had been delivered by judges for four hundred years handed its excuse, and a demand made at Ramah that cost Israel far more than two corrupt men in Beersheba ever took in bribes.

text.text: And it came to pass, when Samuel was old, that he made his sons judges over Israel.
Now the name of his firstborn was Joel; and the name of his second, Abiah: they were judges in Beer–sheba.
And his sons walked not in his ways, but turned aside after lucre, and took bribes, and perverted judgment.
Judges and officers shalt thou make thee in all thy gates, which the Lord thy God giveth thee, throughout thy tribes: and they shall judge the people with just judgment.
Thou shalt not wrest judgment; thou shalt not respect persons, neither take a gift: for a gift doth blind the eyes of the wise, and pervert the words of the righteous.
That which is altogether just shalt thou follow, that thou mayest live, and inherit the land which the Lord thy God giveth thee.
And thou shalt take no gift: for the gift blindeth the wise, and perverteth the words of the righteous.

Behold, here I am: witness against me before the Lord, and before his anointed: whose ox have I taken? or whose ass have I taken? or whom have I defrauded? whom have I oppressed? or of whose hand have I received any bribe to blind mine eyes therewith? and I will restore it you.
And they said, Thou hast not defrauded us, nor oppressed us, neither hast thou taken ought of any man’s hand.
Then all the elders of Israel gathered themselves together, and came to Samuel unto Ramah,
And said unto him, Behold, thou art old, and thy sons walk not in thy ways: now make us a king to judge us like all the nations.
And the Lord said unto Samuel, Hearken unto the voice of the people in all that they say unto thee: for they have not rejected thee, but they have rejected me, that I should not reign over them.

If thou seest the oppression of the poor, and violent perverting of judgment and justice in a province, marvel not at the matter: for he that is higher than the highest regardeth; and there be higher than they.
Judges and officers shalt thou make thee in all thy gates, which the Lord thy God giveth thee, throughout thy tribes: and they shall judge the people with just judgment.
Thou shalt not wrest judgment; thou shalt not respect persons, neither take a gift: for a gift doth blind the eyes of the wise, and pervert the words of the righteous.
